title: Rust: Linked List
description: Implement a singly linked list in Rust using Box for heap allocation.

steps.title: Define List Node
steps.description: Define an enum `List<T>` with variants `Cons(T, Box<List<T>>)` and `Nil`. Create a list containing `[1, 2, 3]` and print with `{:?}`.
hints: `use List::{Cons, Nil};` to bring variants into scope.
Create: `let list = Cons(1, Box::new(Cons(2, Box::new(Cons(3, Box::new(Nil))))));`

verification.failureMessage: Create and print a list of [1, 2, 3].

steps.title: List Length
steps.description: Implement a method `len(&self) -> u32` on List that recursively counts the number of elements.

verification.failureMessage: Print the length of a 3-element list.

steps.title: Push Front
steps.description: Implement a method `push_front(&mut self, value: T)` that adds an element to the front of the list. Demonstrate by pushing 0 to the front of [1, 2, 3].
hints: `let old = std::mem::replace(self, Nil);` to take ownership.
This is needed because you can't move out of &mut self directly.

verification.failureMessage: Push 0 to the front of [1,2,3] and print.

steps.title: To Vec
steps.description: Implement a method `to_vec(&self) -> Vec<&T>` that converts the list to a Vec. Also implement `from_vec(vec: Vec<T>) -> Self` as an associated function.
hints: `to_vec`: recursively traverse and push each element.
`from_vec`: iterate the Vec in reverse and cons each element.
These conversions make testing much easier.

verification.failureMessage: Convert [4,5,6] to List and back to Vec, print result.

steps.title: Pop Front
steps.description: Implement `pop_front(&mut self) -> Option<T>` that removes and returns the first element. Test by popping all elements from [1, 2, 3] until the list is empty.
hints: `match std::mem::replace(self, Nil) { Nil => None, Cons(v, tail) => { *self = *tail; Some(v) } }`
Call pop_front in a while-let loop until None.

verification.successMessage: Pop front works! List fully drained.
verification.failureMessage: Pop all elements from [1,2,3] and print each.
